But if God knows what actions you will perform in the future, there must be truths about what actions you will perform in the future (otherwise there would be nothing for God to know).
To see what Aristotle is thinking, let’s look at two propositions about a possible future free action of yours.
The law of the excluded middle
For any proposition P, either P is true or Not-P is true.
We can put this together into the theological argument for fate.
It is widely held that God is omniscient, and also widely held that (for this reason) God knows what actions you will perform in the future.
So it must be that, if the law of the excluded middle is true, then one of these claims is true, and one of them is false.
